title: A Microfluidic Platform for Stimulating Chondrocytes with Dynamic Compression
protocol: Wear personal protective equipment (PPE) such as gloves and a lab coat for every step in this protocol.
Make Piranha solution by mixing sulfuric acid and hydrogen peroxide with a volume ratio of 3:1.
Place a glass plate in the Piranha solution for 30 min at 40 °C.
Rinse the glass plate with deionized water (diH2O).
Place the glass plate in acetone at room temperature for 10 min.
Rinse the glass plate with isopropanol.
Dry the glass plate with nitrogen (N2) gas.
Bake the glass plate at 200 °C for 20 min on a hot plate.
Spread SU-8 5 on the glass plate with a disposable pipette to cover around 2/3 of the plate’s surface area.
Spin the glass plate with SU-8 5 photoresists at 500 rpm for 35 s (initial spinning cycle).
Spin the glass plate at 2,500 rpm for 40 s using a spin coater.
Bake the SU-8 5 coated glass plate at 65 °C for 2 min.
Bake the SU-8 5 coated glass plate at 95 °C for 5 min.
Expose the SU-8 5 coated glass plate to UV light at 60 mW/cm² for 1 second.
Bake the SU-8 5 coated glass plate at 65 °C for 2 minutes.
Bake the SU-8 5 coated glass plate at 95 °C for 5 minutes.
Place the baked glass plate in the SU-8 developer for 2 minutes.
Bake the SU-8 5 coated glass plate at 180 °C for 20 minutes.
Pour SU-8 100 on the SU-8 5 seeded glass plate to cover approximately two-thirds of the surface area.
Spin the glass plate with SU-8 100 at 3,000 rpm for 38 seconds.
Bake the SU-8 100 coated glass plate at 65 °C for 10 minutes.
Bake the SU-8 100 coated glass plate at 95 °C for 30 minutes.
If necessary, bake the glass plate at 95 °C for a longer period until SU-8 100 is non-sticky.
Place a high-resolution microchannel photomask on the SU-8 100 coated glass plate and expose to UV light for 4 seconds.
Remove the photomask from the glass plate.
Bake the glass plate at 65 °C for 2 minutes.
Bake the glass plate at 95 °C for 20 minutes.
Keep the baked glass plate in a container wrapped with aluminum foil overnight.
Develop SU-8 100 channel patterns on the glass plate in the SU-8 developer for 15 minutes.
Wash the SU-8 patterned glass plate with isopropyl alcohol.
Dry the washed glass plate with N2 gas.
If white particles remain, repeat washing step with isopropyl alcohol and drying with N2 gas for 5 minutes.
Drop 200 μL of (Tridecafluoro-1,1,2,2-Tetrahydrooctyl)-1-Trichlorosilane on a coverslip.
Place the coverslip in a vacuum chamber with the master mold.
Apply vacuum for 2 minutes in the chamber.
Wait for silanization of the mold for 6 hours (or overnight).
Mix PDMS with a weight ratio of 10:1 (prepolymer:curing agent) for 5 minutes.
Pour PDMS on the master mold.
Degas PDMS in a vacuum chamber for 30 minutes.
Sandwich PDMS with a piece of transparency film.
Clamp the sandwiched assembly with a glass plate, foam pads, and plexiglass plates.
Cure PDMS in an oven at 80 °C for 6 hours.
Isolate the PDMS layer (Layer 1) with the transparency film from the sandwiched structure.
Activate surfaces of Layer 1 using a plasma cleaner for 1 minute.
Activate surfaces of a clean glass plate (Glass plate 1; 50.8 mm × 76.2 mm × 1.2 mm) using a plasma cleaner for 1 minute.
Bond Layer 1 onto Glass plate 1.
Place the bonded structure in the oven at 80 °C for 30 minutes.
Remove the transparency film from Layer 1.
Spin coat uncured PDMS on a transparency film at 1,000 rpm for 1 minute to obtain a 60 μm thick PDMS layer.
Partially cure spin coated PDMS (Layer 2) in the oven at 80 °C for 20-30 minutes.
Activate Layer 1 and Layer 2 using the plasma cleaner for 1 minute.
Bond the Layer 2 onto Layer 1 and place them in the oven at 80 °C overnight.
Place metal tubes vertically on a petri dish.
Gently pour PDMS into the dish to submerge about 3/4 of the metal tubes.
Cure PDMS in the oven at 60 °C for 6 hours (or overnight).
Cut a piece of PDMS block containing one metal tube.
Punch a hole on Layer 2 for the inlet.
Activate the PDMS block and Layer 2 using the plasma cleaner for 1 minute.
Attach the PDMS block onto the inlet part of Layer 2.
Place the entire actuation unit in the oven at 80 °C overnight.
Cut a glass plate (50.8 mm × 76.2 mm × 1.2 mm) into two half-sized glass plates (50.8 mm × 38.1 mm × 1.2 mm).
Place the glass plates in 0.2 M hydrogen chloride (HCl) and gently shake overnight.
Rinse the glass plates with diH2O.
Shake the glass plates in 0.1 M sodium hydroxide (NaOH) for 1 hour at 55 rpm.
Rinse them with diH2O.
Shake glass plates in 1% (v/v) 3-aminopropyltrimethoxysilane (APTES) for 1 hour at 55 rpm.
Rinse amino-silanized glass plates with diH2O.
Dry the amino-silanized glass plates in a fume hood overnight.
Mix 5% (w/v) agarose and 200 mM calcium chloride (CaCl2) in diH2O.
Boil the agarose gel solution.
Pour boiled agarose gel solution onto an aluminum mold.
Wait for 5 minutes.
Unmold solidified agarose gel from the aluminum mold.
Isolate growth plates from the hind limbs of neonatal mice.
Place growth plates in 1 mL of 0.25% collagenase.
Incubate the sample at 37 °C and 8% carbon dioxide (CO2) for 3 hours to remove extracellular matrix (ECM).
Centrifuge the digested sample for 5 minutes at 125 x g to make a chondrocyte pellet.
Remove supernatant from the sample.
Resuspend the chondrocyte pellet in 1 mL of Dulbecco's modified Eagle's medium (DMEM).
Count the number of chondrocytes in DMEM using a cell counter.
Centrifuge the chondrocytes in DMEM for 5 minutes at 125 x g to make another chondrocyte pellet.
Remove supernatant from the sample.
Resuspend the chondrocyte pellet in CCM containing 2 μM calcein AM.
Incubate the sample at 37 °C for 30 min.
Mix 1.5% (w/v) alginate in PBS with 5 mg/mL of sulfo-NHS and 10 mg/mL of EDC.
Add 8 x 10^6 chondrocytes into 1 mL of the alginate gel solution.
Place 150 μL of the alginate-chondrocyte solution on an amino-silanized glass plate.
Cover the alginate gel solution with an agarose gel mold for 3 min.
Remove excessive alginate gel solution overflowing from the agarose gel mold with a razor blade and remove the agarose gel mold.
Place the alginate-chondrocyte constructs in cross-linking solution (50 mM CaCl2 / 140 mM NaCl) for 1 min.
Place 700 μL of CCM to cover the air chambers of Layer 2.
Place alginate-chondrocyte (or bead) constructs on Layer 2 while carefully aligning with the air chambers.
Clamp the device with 3D printed clamps.
Connect the outlet of an air pump with the inlet of a solenoid valve using silicon tubing.
Connect the outlet of the solenoid valve with the inlet of the assembled device using silicon tubing.
Connect the solenoid valve to a function generator.
Manipulate the solenoid valve with a square wave generated by the function generator.
Turn on the air pump to actuate the device pneumatically.
Image chondrocytes (or fluorescent beads) in alginate gel through Glass plate 2.
Take z-stack images of chondrocytes (or fluorescent beads) before and under compression.
Choose a z-step size based on the depth of field of the used confocal imaging system.
